fact: Eight local authorities were onboarded onto the Government Services Bus from June 2026, letting residents and businesses pay property rates, business levies and permits electronically, per the Zambian Business Times.
The Ministry of Finance and National Planning data cited say about K21.7 million was collected through the Government Services Bus in the month since the June 2026 rollout to eight councils.

ZamPay and ZamPortal let citizens and businesses pay for more than 400 government services electronically, including passport applications and road tax, by bank transfer, card and mobile money, per the Office of the Accountant General.
The Office of the Accountant General says Zambia's digital payment and service platforms have collected more than K8.8 billion (US$488 million).
The National Road Fund Agency takes toll fees by mobile money through Lipila at toll gates across the country, with over 40,000 transactions in about two months of rollout, per Hobbiton and the NRFA.
